PullRequest.Title: build: move the native build targets from .npmrc to package.json
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to the pnpm 12 migration (#344791), from its review feedback: drop the `.npmrc` files that only held native-build settings.

## What changed

After the migration, the `.npmrc` files of the root, `build` and `remote` only held node-gyp and prebuild-install settings (`target`, `runtime`, `disturl`, `ms_build_id`, `build_from_source`, `force_process_config`). pnpm ignores them there, and npm 11 warns that they will stop working. This PR moves them to a typed `nativeBuild` field in each install root's `package.json` and deletes the three `.npmrc` files. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can't hold them, because pnpm 12 fails on unknown settings.

```jsonc
// package.json
"nativeBuild": { "runtime": "electron", "target": "43.8.6", "disturl": "https://electronjs.org/headers", "msBuildId": "15893748", "buildFromSource": true }
// remote/package.json
"nativeBuild": { "runtime": "node", "target": "24.22.1", "disturl": "https://nodejs.org/dist", "msBuildId": "488038", "buildFromSource": true, "forceProcessConfig": true }
// build/package.json (no target: it builds for the running Node.js, as before)
"nativeBuild": { "runtime": "node", "disturl": "https://nodejs.org/dist", "buildFromSource": true, "forceProcessConfig": true }
```

- **One definition:** the field is described once, as `NativeBuildConfig` in `build/npm/pnpm/nativeBuildEnv.ts`. `readNativeBuildConfig` checks it and fails on an unknown property, a wrong type or a missing `runtime`/`disturl`. The `.pnpmfile.mjs` hooks still turn it into the same `npm_config_*` variables.
- **Typed readers:** `getElectronVersion()` (`build/lib/electronVersion.ts`, same return shape as before, so the distro mixins keep working) and the new `getServerNodeVersion()`/`getServerNodePath()` (`build/lib/node.ts`; running it as a script still prints the path).
- **Readers switched:**
  - install: preinstall header downloads, postinstall (distro remote root), `installStateHash.ts`, `cloudSandboxSetup.ts`;
  - build: `gulpfile.reh.ts`, `darwin/sign.ts`, `useRunnerNodeForServer.ts`;
  - CI: the Alpine pipelines read the field with `node -p` inside the existing step, with no new steps;
  - tests: `scripts/test.sh`, `scripts/test.bat`, `test/unit/node/index.js`.
- **`force_process_config`:** in `build/.npmrc` it had no effect, because a pnpmfile option always overrode it. The field now controls it (still macOS only), and that option is removed. `remote/package.json` sets it too, so its builds stay the same.
- **Caches:**
  - The `node_modules` cache key hashes only selected sections of each `package.json`, so it now also hashes `nativeBuild`.
  - The base key that pull requests start from when their own `node_modules` cache is missing (`computeNodeModulesBaseCacheKey`, #345840) used to hash the `.npmrc` files; it now hashes the `nativeBuild` fields instead, so a runtime bump doesn't reuse modules built for the old runtime.
  - The GitHub Electron download cache is keyed on `build/checksums/electron.txt` alone. Every Electron bump changes that file, and `msBuildId` doesn't affect those downloads.
- **Install-state hash:** the local install-state hash (`build/npm/installStateHash.ts`) also keeps only selected `package.json` keys, so `nativeBuild` is added there too: changing the field makes the next install run again.
- **Change detection:** `detect-changes`, `detect-agent-host-e2e-changes` and ripple no longer list the `.npmrc` files.
- **Packaging:** the shipped desktop and server `package.json` files don't include `nativeBuild`.
- **Lockfiles:** the three `.pnpmfile.mjs` files changed (comments, and the removed option), so each lockfile's `pnpmfileChecksum` changes. That is the only lockfile change.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Electron and Node.js bumps** now edit `nativeBuild.target`/`msBuildId` in `package.json` (Electron) or `remote/package.json` (Node.js), together with `build/checksums/*.txt` and `cgmanifest.json` as before. Tooling outside this repo that opens bump PRs needs updating.
- **ripple:** it can't single out the `nativeBuild` field, so it relies on the checksum files.
  - Electron and Node.js bumps still run every unit test, through `build/checksums/electron.txt`, and now also `build/checksums/nodejs.txt`.
  - An `msBuildId`-only change selects the tests that read `package.json` instead of all tests. A `remote` target change without a `nodejs.txt` update selects none.
- **Out of scope:** release branches (they stay on npm), the distro's npm folders (they still get `remote`'s values from the environment through `postinstall.ts`), and `build/agent-sdk/agents/*`.

## How to test

All validation was on macOS arm64 with Node.js 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.16.0.

- After `git clean -fdX`, `PNPM_CONFIG_FROZEN_LOCKFILE=true pnpm install` succeeds, with the same install-script results as `main`.
- **Native build environment:** the `.pnpmfile.mjs` hooks produce the same environment as `main` in all 18 cases tried (darwin/linux/win32 × root/build/remote, with and without an inherited Electron environment), checked again after rebasing on `main` with Electron 43.8.6. The distro's `remote` environment from `postinstall.ts` is the same as on `main` too.
- **Native module parity:**
  - Rebuilding a module without any change already gives a different `.node` file here, so the binaries can't be compared byte for byte.
  - Instead, all 32 `build/config.gypi` files are byte-identical to a fresh `main` install. They show Electron (ABI 148) for the root and Copilot, Node.js 24.22.1 (ABI 137) for `remote` and `build`, and the `process.config` settings only for `remote` and `build`.
- **Version readers:** `getElectronVersion()` and `getServerNodeVersion()` return the same values as before. `pnpm run gulp node` downloads Node.js 24.22.1 and checks it against `build/checksums/nodejs.txt`.
- **Checks:**
  - `npm run typecheck` in `build` passes.
  - The `build/npm/**` tests pass, and so do the `build/lib` tests for electronVersion, cloudSandbox, detectChanges, detectMissingCaches, agentHostTestSelection, useRunnerNodeForServer, darwinSign and nodeGypHeaders.
  - ESLint reports no problems in the changed files.
  - In the full `build` suite, `build/next/test/resources.test.ts` fails the same way on `main` (macOS `/private/var` vs `/var` temporary paths).
- **Pipelines:** the Azure template preview of the product build succeeds with default parameters and with `VSCODE_PUBLISH=false`. It has the same number of steps as `main`, and no builds were queued.
- **Not verified:** Windows (including the `test.bat` change), Linux and the Alpine container installs, and a full product build.

Scenarios.Scenario: Root dependency install and native-module configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a warm unchanged tree, install-state hashing completes and preinstall exits before header setup. On a cold or invalidated install, the preinstall's gyp install and two runtime-header installs must finish before dependency installation can proceed; later separate native roots are installed sequentially as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and JSON-parse package.json/remote/package.json for nativeBuild settings instead of reading and regex-parsing .npmrc files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two manifest reads in cold preinstall plus one read per pnpm install-root hook process; independent of dependency count because updateConfig computes extraEnv once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same paths synchronously read small .npmrc files; the diff changes the source and parsing format, not boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous reads are on cold-install setup, but replace equivalent synchronous configuration-file reads and are negligible beside package installation and native compilation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the pinned node-gyp package, then run node-gyp to install Electron and server Node.js headers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pnpm subprocess and two sequential node-gyp subprocesses on a cold/invalidated install; cached headers may avoid network transfer inside node-gyp.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical subprocess count and ordering; only dist URL and target lookup moved from .npmrc to package.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations block cold install before dependency installation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download Electron and Node.js headers through node-gyp on cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two logical header installs per cold preinstall, each with the existing retry policy; effective target count remains two.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two targets and URLs were read from .npmrc and downloaded on the same path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold cache misses block install; warm node-gyp caches avoid the downloads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of install roots is fixed and small; dependency count does not multiply manifest parsing or header downloads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The Electron and server Node.js header subprocesses remain sequential. Postinstall native roots remain sequential to avoid node-gyp conflicts, while JS-only roots retain the existing CPU-count limiter capped at 8. The pnpm updateConfig hook reads one manifest once per install-root pnpm process, not once per dependency script.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The warm install-state fast path remains before header setup. Adding nativeBuild to the normalized install-state input intentionally invalidates after runtime configuration changes; unrelated package.json fields remain excluded. Header caches continue to key internally by target.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call sites, ordering, hook lifetime, and unchanged two-target header boundary are explicit in the code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact JSON parse cost varies with manifest size, but call count is fixed and the work replaces configuration parsing on an already expensive cold path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: expensive subprocess/network work and concurrency are unchanged, while added manifest parsing is bounded and one-time per root.

Scenarios.Scenario: CI node_modules and Electron cache-key computation/restoration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Local synchronous file hashing must finish before cache restore keys are available; subsequent cache restore/download behavior depends on the resulting keys.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read package manifests and native-build hook files to compute node_modules keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The main key already reads each of roughly 60 workspace/install-root package.json files once. The base-key helper now reads the same fixed directory list to extract nativeBuild, but repository search finds no production caller in this revision beyond tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The main key read the same manifests but omitted nativeBuild from the selected object. The base helper read three .npmrc files rather than the fixed manifest list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Main key hashing is required before restore; base-key work is not currently on a production workflow path in this revision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore an Electron download cache and download Electron archives on a cold cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache restore and one logical Electron download setup per job, unchanged; the key now hashes one checksum file instead of the checksum plus .npmrc.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cache action and download ran; .npmrc contributed to the key. The checksum file changes with every Electron target bump, preserving target invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache misses can block setup, while warm hits avoid archive downloads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed repository package count for filesystem hashing and one cache operation per job; no per-dependency network fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cache-key file reads and hashing are sequential in one Node.js process. Cache actions remain one logical restore per cache; no loop adds parallel network requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Electron cache remains keyed by OS, architecture, and Electron checksum inventory, so target changes still miss and ordinary manifest changes no longer cause false misses. node_modules keys now include nativeBuild, preventing reuse of binaries built for a different runtime. No negative cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for key composition and file-read cardinality; high that the base helper has no non-test caller in this revision.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future use of the base-key helper could add roughly one manifest read per listed directory, but current production reachability is absent and the bounded local work is small compared with cache restore/install.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: cache invalidation becomes more precise, network cardinality is unchanged, and the only added filesystem scan is bounded and not currently on a production path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build, package, sign, and test launch runtime-version resolution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Runtime version lookup occurs once during each affected script's startup before signing, packaging, downloading runtimes, or launching tests can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Electron or server Node.js version from package.json in shell/CI scripts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One version-resolution command per script invocation. Alpine reduces two pipeline processes to one Node process; test launch remains one external command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unix tests used one sed command, Windows used findstr, and Alpine used grep piped to cut. The diff substitutes a single Node process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command is on script startup, but fixed-cardinality and followed by much larger test/build work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Locate the server Node.js binary for CI reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero nested subprocesses after the diff; direct helper calls replace one execFileSync Node process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Spawned one Node subprocess to execute build/lib/node.ts, then separately read remote/.npmrc.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removes process startup from the CI setup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch Electron/server Node.js archives during build tasks when absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime artifact per requested platform/architecture task, unchanged by the version reader refactor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same target and internal build IDs selected the same artifact fetches; only their checked-in source moved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold artifact fetches block their build tasks; existing caches serve warm runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read package.json to obtain nativeBuild and remove nativeBuild while generating shipped manifests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or a few fixed reads/JSON edits per build-script invocation or packaged product, not per source file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Version readers synchronously read tiny .npmrc files, and package editors did not need to remove nativeBuild because the field did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded setup work before substantially heavier packaging/signing operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of script invocations and build platform/architecture tasks; version parsing is constant per invocation and does not scale with source-tree size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each script resolves versions synchronously once. Alpine commands run one node process instead of a grep/cut pipeline; Unix and Windows test launchers run one node process where they previously invoked sed or findstr. useRunnerNodeForServer removes a nested Node subprocess and performs direct reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Runtime artifact cache targets remain the same. Generated desktop/server manifests explicitly omit nativeBuild, avoiding shipped metadata growth. Warm installed-Electron checks still compare the same target value.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all command substitutions and direct-helper call paths are visible in changed lines.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Node startup is heavier than sed/findstr on test launch, but it occurs once before a full suite and is partly offset in Alpine and CI helper paths; no realistic user-visible regression is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: all added work is constant startup overhead on heavyweight build/test workflows, while one existing subprocess is removed and artifact boundary cardinality is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 46 changed files and all diff pages. Traced install, native-header, cache-key, runtime-fetch, packaging, signing, and test-launch paths. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
